Website · GitHub · The guide · ☕ Buy me a Coffee Machine

> Ruach Studio is open music generation that runs on your own hardware: the model, the score, the adapters and every take stay yours, and nothing is rented by the token. Open models are now good enough to stand on their own, and what was missing is the studio around them: that is what we build, in the open. Music should be free to make and to share: whoever has no voice, no instrument and no studio still has the right to lay their thoughts and feelings onto sound. > **⚠ Not on free cloud GPUs.** Ruach Studio does not run on Google Colab, Kaggle or any free notebook GPU, so don't spend an evening on it there: it is a whole studio, not a notebook. It builds its C++/CUDA engine on the machine it lives on, keeps a server and a lab of Python services running beside it, and takes about 33 GB of disk (60 GB with the Artist). A free session's card, memory, wiped disk and hours-long limit cannot hold that. It wants your own Linux computer, or a server you rent and keep, with an NVIDIA card: 24 GB for everything, 16 GB with the smaller model copies. Everything [Ruach Studio](https://github.com/igrbible/Ruach_Studio) runs on, in one place and laid out as its own folders: the music model and its decoders, the transcriber, the stems' and the sound upscaler's models, Whisper, the style listener, the studio's own adapters, the LoRA Trainer's base, and the Artist's painters with the adapters their authors let be shared. 1662 files, 501 GB. A copy of the studio's own disk, file for file: what lies here is what it paints, sings and trains with, and the studio fetches all of it from here alone. **Nothing here is ours but the conversions and the studio's own adapters.** Every other file is its authors' work, unchanged, under its authors' licence, credited below and line by line in `MANIFEST.tsv`. Not affiliated with M-A-P, Comfy Org, Mothersuperior, HaileyStorm, atomtanstudio, storagejuju, OpenAI, Systran, Meta, the Qwen team, Unsloth, lightx2v, Falconsai, prithivMLmods, Civitai or the authors named below. If you are an author and want a file of yours taken down, open a discussion here and it goes. ## Take what you need The studio's own install (`./fetch-models.sh`) takes what your card can run, at a pinned revision, checking each file. By hand, from the studio's root: ```bash hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "models/YuE2-3B-Q8_0.gguf" "models/YuE2-Vae-F32.gguf" "models/SheetSage2-Q8_0.gguf" "models/MERT-v2-FullSong-Q8_0.gguf" # to sing: 5.3 GB hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "models/YuE2-Vae-*" # the other decoders hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "models/SheetSage2-Refined-F16.gguf" "models/SheetSage2-Refined/*" # the second transcriber (beside SheetSage2): 0.16 GB hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "whisper/*" "separation/*" "universr/*" # Whisper, stems, the sound's upscaler hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "artwork/upscalers/*" "licenses/upscalers/*" # the Artist's upscalers hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/gguf/*Q4_K_M*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/lightning/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/*.json" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/scheduler/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/tokenizer/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/text_encoder/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/vae/*" "artwork/Qwen-Image-2512/transformer/*" # the Artist on 16 GB hf download goldhub/Ruach_Studio_Models_v2 --local-dir . --include "checkpoints/comfy/checkpoints/yue2_3b_bf16.safetensors" "checkpoints/MERT-v2-FullSong/*" "checkpoints/yue2-mothersuperior-realaudio-tokenizer-v4/*" # the LoRA Trainer's base: 10.5 GB ``` ## Known by its content, not its name `SHA256SUMS` holds each file's SHA-256 (as `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` reads it, and as Hugging Face knows the file). `MANIFEST.tsv` adds, for each `.safetensors`, the SHA-256 of its tensors alone (their names and data, its header's metadata aside), with each file's origin and licence. Sori-10B-Speech

Seonuk Kim  ·  Semin Kim  ·  Beom Jun Woo  ·  🇰🇷
{sukim, smkim21, bjwoo}@hi.snu.ac.kr

*Sori* (소리) is Korean for *sound*. Sori-10B-Speech is a speech LLM that hears how things are said (tone, hesitation, emotion, who is speaking and in what state) and uses those cues when it reasons. ## Usage ```python # pip install "transformers>=5.23" soundfile import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoProcessor repo = "snkii/Sori-10B-Speech" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto") audio, sr = sf.read("speech.wav", dtype="float32") # 16 kHz mono messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio"}, {"type": "text", "text": "How does the speaker sound, and why?"}, ]}] prompt = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False) inputs = processor(text=prompt, audio=audio, sampling_rate=sr, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device) output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) print(processor.decode(output[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)) ``` Reasoning before answering: the model first writes down what it hears, then answers. ```python prompt = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False, enable_thinking=True) inputs = processor(text=prompt, audio=audio, sampling_rate=sr, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device) output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, do_sample=True, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20) text = processor.decode(output[0, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True) reasoning, _, answer = text.partition("") print(answer.strip()) ``` Several clips and questions in one batch: ```python files = ["a.wav", "b.wav", "c.wav"] questions = ["How does the speaker sound, and why?", "What is the speaker's mood?", "Is the speaker hesitant?"] audios = [sf.read(f, dtype="float32")[0] for f in files] # 16 kHz mono prompts = [processor.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "audio"}, {"type": "text", "text": q}, ]}], add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False) for q in questions] inputs = processor(text=prompts, audio=audios, sampling_rate=16000, padding=True, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device) output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) for answer in processor.batch_decode(output[:, inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True): print(answer) ``` ## License Sori-10B-Speech is released under **[CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/)**: use it and build on it for non-commercial purposes, with attribution, and share what you derive from it under the same terms. # HeartMuLa-oss-3B for mlx-serve (8bit)

[HeartMuLa-oss-3B](https://huggingface.co/HeartMuLa/HeartMuLa-oss-3B-happy-new-year) with
[HeartCodec](https://huggingface.co/HeartMuLa/HeartCodec-oss-20260123), converted for

song out.

LM: affine 8-bit, group 64, on every matmul and both embedding tables. Codec: DiT bf16, the rest f32.

Run it in [MLX-Serve.app](https://github.com/ddalcu/mlx-serve/releases/latest) (Music tab) or over HTTP. Tags are
lowercase and comma-separated without spaces; structure tags like `[Verse]` go on their own lines in the lyrics.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:11234/v1/audio/music-generations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -o song.wav -d '{
  "model": "HeartMuLa-3B-MLX-Serve-8bit", "prompt": "pop,piano,female vocal,upbeat",
  "lyrics": "[Verse]\nneon lights across the bay\n[Chorus]\nwe run all night", "duration_seconds": 60}'
```

Rebuild with `scripts/convert_heartmula_weights.py`. Apache-2.0, as upstream.

Not fp16: the backbone's residual stream reaches 4e4 on real prompts (3e4 from the third layer on), and an fp16 build overflows to NaN on the first prefill. `embed.onnx` makes its input embeddings from text token ids. - `patch_encoder.onnx`: latent frames -> one backbone embedding per patch of 4 RedAE frames (1/6.25 s). - `flow_step.onnx`: one velocity evaluation of the diffusion transformer (flow matching) with classifier-free guidance. - `heads.onnx`: hidden states -> the DiT's condition and the stop probability. - `speaker.onnx` (the prompt's fbank -> CAM++ embedding and its backbone / DiT projections), `redae_encoder.onnx` (24 kHz audio -> latents, 25 frames / s), `redae_decoder.onnx` (latents -> the iSTFT's windowed frames, overlap-added in numpy). `pipeline.py` runs the original's loop with its defaults (10 Euler steps on a cosine schedule, CFG 2.0, stop threshold 0.5 after at least 6 patches, at most 400) and decodes. On CUDA the backbone's cache is one fixed buffer per layer, written in place. It needs numpy, onnxruntime (or onnxruntime-gpu), onnx, tokenizers and soundfile: ```bash python fp16/pipeline.py "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." --language English --prompt-audio voice.wav \ --prompt-text "Exactly what is said in voice.wav." --out out.wav --low-memory ``` ```python import sys, soundfile as sf sys.path.insert(0, "fp16") import onnxruntime as ort import pipeline ort.preload_dlls() # onnxruntime-gpu with pip CUDA / cuDNN tts = pipeline.FireRedTTS3("fp16", providers=["CUDAExecutionProvider", "CPUExecutionProvider"], low_memory=True, cpu_graphs=("speaker", "redae_encoder", "embed")) wav = tts.generate("Text to say.", "English", "voice.wav", "Transcript of voice.wav.", seed=0) # 24 kHz sf.write("out.wav", wav, 24000) ``` Not included: core.FireRedTTS3's text front end (cleaning, language detection, wetext normalisation, splitting long text into sentences and cross-fading them). Give the language, text a sentence or two at a time, numbers written out. The diffusion noise comes from numpy's generator, so a seed gives the same speech every run here, not the same speech as PyTorch with that seed. **Memory and speed.** `low_memory=True` holds one stage's graphs at a time (prompt, generate, decode) and loads them for each call; `cpu_graphs` runs the small prompt graphs and the embedding table on the CPU. That is how the benchmark ran: one clip peaks at 6.2 GB of process memory (fp16, CUDA) or 3.7 GB (int4). Of 24 s for a 6 s clip in fp16, 13 s is loading the graphs, 8 s the DiT (370 velocity evaluations), 1 s RedAE's encoder and under 1 s the backbone. cuDNN, which RedAE's decoder loads, stays in the process for about 1 GB after its graphs are released; the benchmark ran one clip per process. **Precisions.** `fp16/`: the backbone in bfloat16 (above); the DiT, patch encoder and heads in fp16 arithmetic (the DiT's 1-D convolutions written as MatMuls); CAM++ and RedAE fp16 weights with fp32 math; the embedding table fp16. `int4/`: the backbone 4-bit MatMulNBits (block 32, bfloat16 scales and activations), the DiT, patch encoder, heads and RedAE's matmuls 4-bit and their other weights int8, the embedding table int8 per row, CAM++ as in `fp16/`. No int8 or fp16-backbone build. **Benchmark.** The lab's TTS set: 6 English sentences cloned from a LibriSpeech test-clean prompt and 4 Chinese sentences from an AISHELL-1 prompt, each with seeds 0 and 1 (20 clips per build), the original's defaults. Sampled speech can't be compared sample by sample, so each build is judged as the original is: Whisper large-v3-turbo's WER (English) or CER (Chinese) against the text, WavLM-base-plus-sv speaker similarity to the prompt, and DNSMOS (P.835 overall). The original is FireRedTTS3Base.generate (github.com/FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3 @7a1f3a7) as it runs on CUDA: the backbone and RedAE's encoder under bfloat16 autocast, the rest float32. FireRedTTS3: Unified Speech Generation and Editing with Semantically Enriched Speech Representations

## Overview **FireRedTTS3** is a unified speech generation and editing system built on **semantically enriched continuous speech representations**. It comes in two variants: - **FireRedTTS3-Base** — zero-shot voice cloning across **24 languages** and **21 Chinese dialects** - **FireRedTTS3-Instruct** — natural-language **voice design** and **speech editing** (semantic + acoustic) in one unified model ## Highlights ✨ * 🌍 **Multilingual — 24 Languages** — Best average WER/CER (avg 3.754%) and best average speaker similarity on MiniMax-MLS-Test (avg 84.8%), plus best-in-class cloning WER/CER (avg 3.04%) and similarity on Seed-TTS-eval (avg 78.8%). Supported languages: `Arabic` · `Cantonese` · `Chinese` · `Czech` · `Dutch` · `English` · `Finnish` · `French` · `German` · `Greek` · `Hindi` · `Indonesian` · `Italian` · `Japanese` · `Korean` · `Polish` · `Portuguese` · `Romanian` · `Russian` · `Spanish` · `Thai` · `Turkish` · `Ukrainian` · `Vietnamese` * 🗣️ **Multi-Dialect — 21 Chinese Dialects** — Zero-shot voice cloning across major Chinese dialect groups. Supported dialects: `Anhui` · `Fujian` · `Gansu` · `Guizhou` · `Hebei` · `Henan` · `Hubei` · `Hunan` · `Jiangxi` · `Liaoning` · `Minnan` · `Ningxia` · `Shaanxi` · `Shandong` · `Shanghai` · `Shanxi` · `Sichuan` · `Tianjin` · `Wenzhou` · `Wu` · `Yunnan` * 🎨 **Instruction-Controlled Voice Design** — Generate a brand-new voice from a natural-language description (gender, age, timbre, emotion, pace, accent…) with no reference audio, guided by an explicit textual plainning step before synthesis. * ✂️ **Free-Form Speech Editing** — Semantic editing (insertion / deletion / substitution) and acoustic editing (speed / pitch / volume) driven by free-form instructions. ## News - [2026.08.05] We release **FireRedTTS3-Base** - [2026.08.13] We release the **FireRedTTS3-Instruct** model & code ## Roadmap - [x] Release the FireRedTTS3-Base model - [x] Release the FireRedTTS3-Instruct model - [x] Release the technical report ## Contents - [Quick Start](#-quick-start) - [Model](#-model) - [Performance](#-performance) - [Usage Disclaimer](#-usage-disclaimer-) - [Citation](#-citation) - [Acknowledgements](#-acknowledgements) - [License](#-license) ## Quick Start 🚀 ### Clone the repo ```sh git clone https://github.com/FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3.git cd FireRedTTS3 ``` ### Installation with pip ```sh pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### Model Download Download the pretrained model from Hugging Face with the `hf` CLI: ```sh pip install "huggingface_hub[cli]" hf download FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3 --local-dir pretrained_models/ ``` Alternatively, you can download model from ModelScope ```sh pip install modelscope modelscope download --model FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3 --local_dir pretrained_models/ ``` ### Configure Text Frontend #### Language Recognition (Optional) FireRedTTS3-Base relies on explicit language tags for best performance. However, if you don't know the exact language of the text, you can download Meta's `FastText` language-id model and let it detect the language automatically. ```sh # Download FastText language-id model (lid.176) with: curl -L -o fireredtts3/utils/llm_tn/models/lid.176.ftz https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/fasttext/supervised-models/lid.176.ftz ``` #### Text Normalization (TN) TN converts written numbers, dates, units, currencies, acronyms, etc. into their spoken form (e.g. 19:30 → nineteen thirty). By default, FireRedTTS3 uses the `wetext` TN tool, which supports Chinese and English, other languages (e.g. Japanese, Russian) undergo only basic cleaning. For full language TN support, enable the LLM-based TN by passing `use_llm_tn=True` when initializing FireRedTTS3. It reads its config from a .env file: ```sh cp .env.example .env # Then fill in your values LLM_TN_API_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions # any OpenAI-compatible endpoint LLM_TN_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx LLM_TN_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash # or any model >= 30B ``` ### Python API For the best voice cloning performance, use a prompt in the desired language or dialect, since the output inherits the speaking style of the reference. For example, provide a Japanese prompt when synthesizing Japanese and a Sichuanese prompt when synthesizing Sichuanese. ```python import torch import torchaudio from fireredtts3.core import FireRedTTS3 # Init model: choose the text-normalization frontend here. # use_wetext=True -> local weText TN (zh/en only) # use_llm_tn=True -> LLM-based TN (all languages, needs .env / API creds) # both False -> no TN frontend built tts = FireRedTTS3( "pretrained_models", use_wetext=True, use_llm_tn=False, ) language = None # Automatic detection if pass None prompt_text = "" prompt_audio, prompt_audio_sr = torchaudio.load('prompt.wav') text = "今天天气很好，我们一起去公园散步吧。" gen_audio, gen_audio_sr = tts.generate( language=language, prompt_text=prompt_text, prompt_audio=prompt_audio, prompt_audio_sr=prompt_audio_sr, text=text, do_tn=True, # whether to run the frontend TN on this call ) torchaudio.save("gen.wav", gen_audio.cpu(), gen_audio_sr) # Supported languages and dialects # Multilingual languages: # Arabic, Cantonese, Chinese, Czech, Dutch, English, Finnish, # French, German, Greek, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, # Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Thai, # Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese # Multi-dialect: # ZH_Anhui, ZH_Fujian, ZH_Gansu, ZH_Guizhou, ZH_Hebei, ZH_Henan, # ZH_Hubei, ZH_Hunan, ZH_Jiangxi, ZH_Liaoning, ZH_Minnan, ZH_Ningxia, # ZH_Shaanxi, ZH_Shandong, ZH_Shanghai, ZH_Shanxi, ZH_Sichuan, # ZH_Tianjin, ZH_Wenzhou, ZH_Wu, ZH_Yunnan ``` ### Instruct API — Voice Design & Speech Editing **FireRedTTS3-Instruct** is a unified instruction-driven model. On top of zero-shot voice cloning, it also supports **Voice Design**, **Semantic Edit** and **Acoustic Edit** through a single entry point: `fireredtts3.core.FireRedTTS3Instruct`. ```python import torch import torchaudio from fireredtts3.core import FireRedTTS3Instruct # Init the Instruct model (same text-frontend options as FireRedTTS3) instruct = FireRedTTS3Instruct( "pretrained_models", use_wetext=True, use_llm_tn=False, # set True to enable LLM-based TN (all languages) ) # ---- 1) Voice Design Inference --------------- # Generate a brand-new voice from a natural-language description only; # no reference audio is needed. The model first writes a voice-attribute # plan (returned as gen_text), then renders the audio. instruction = "一个年轻女性的温柔嗓音，语速稍慢，带一点俏皮。" text = "今天天气很好，我们一起去公园散步吧。" gen_audio, gen_audio_sr, gen_text = instruct.generate_voice_design( instruction=instruction, text=text, ) torchaudio.save("design.wav", gen_audio.cpu(), gen_audio_sr) print("Voice plan:", gen_text) # ---- 2) Semantic Edit ------------------------ # Content-level editing: insertion / deletion / substitution by instruction. # Returns the edited audio and the model's rewritten text with edit mask. audio_in, audio_in_sr = torchaudio.load("input.wav") gen_audio, gen_audio_sr, gen_text = instruct.generate_semantic_edit( instruction="Replace 'cats' with 'dogs'.", audio_in=audio_in, audio_in_sr=audio_in_sr, ) torchaudio.save("edit_semantic.wav", gen_audio.cpu(), gen_audio_sr) print("Edited text:", gen_text) # ---- 3) Acoustic Edit ------------------------ # Acoustic-attribute editing: speed / pitch / volume. The instruction must # follow the trained templates below (free-form phrasing is not supported): # speed -> "adjust the speed to X" X in [0.5, 2.0], step 0.1 # pitch -> "shift the pitch by N step(s)" N in {-6,...,-1,1,...,+6} # volume -> "adjust the volume to X" X in [0.3, 2.0], step 0.1 gen_audio, gen_audio_sr = instruct.generate_acoustic_edit( instruction="adjust the speed to 0.5x", audio_in=audio_in, audio_in_sr=audio_in_sr, ) torchaudio.save("edit_acoustic.wav", gen_audio.cpu(), gen_audio_sr) # ---- 4) ICL zero-shot voice cloning using the Instruct model ---- gen_audio, gen_audio_sr = instruct.generate_tts( prompt_text="", prompt_audio=prompt_audio, prompt_audio_sr=prompt_audio_sr, text="", ) torchaudio.save("gen_instruct.wav", gen_audio.cpu(), gen_audio_sr) ``` ## Performance ### Zero-Shot Voice Cloning — Seed-TTS-eval Best in **bold**, second best in underline. --- language: - en - zh - de - fr - ko - ja - nl - es - it - pt - pl pipeline_tag: text-to-speech tags: - arxiv:2611.30723 - speech-tokenization - audio-tokenizer - speech-codec - text-to-speech - zero-shot-tts - speech-language-model - flow-matching --- # BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models

> **🎧 Listen to Live Audio Demos:** **[https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/](https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/)** *(zero-shot TTS & speech reconstruction samples)* > > **Open-Source Release Coming Soon:** This is the public paper companion repository for **BiSAT** (`arXiv:2611.30723`). We are actively preparing the public release of both **source code** and **pretrained checkpoints** for **BiSAT** (`BiSAT-32k`, `BiSAT-64k`) and **BiSAT-TTS** (`BiSAT-TTS-32k`, `BiSAT-TTS-64k`). Like this repository or follow [SeekMind Lab](https://huggingface.co/seekmind-lab) to be notified as soon as they drop! --- ## 1. Beyond Reconstruction: Why Code Structure Matters When building an autoregressive (AR) speech language model, we want a **single-stream, low-bitrate speech tokenizer** that preserves both linguistic structure and acoustic detail. Yet clean reconstruction WER alone can hide poorly structured discrete tokens: ![Reconstruction vs Frozen-Code Probes](assets/recon_vs_understanding.png) - On clean LibriSpeech-PC reconstruction, `X-Codec2` (50 Hz, 800 bps, adversarial waveform decoder) nearly matches `BiSAT-32k` (25 Hz, 375 bps, *no* adversarial training): **2.27% vs. 2.15% WER**. - Yet on **frozen-code probes**, `X-Codec2` degrades sharply (**8.82% vs. 1.92% PR PER**, **87.7% vs. 24.4% zero-shot FLEURS EN WER**, **5.6% vs. 40.4% VoxCeleb1 SID**, **23.6% vs. 95.5% LID**). - Purely semantic tokenizers (`CosyVoice 2/3`) preserve content well but trail on speaker cues (**24.7%–24.8% SID**); purely acoustic codecs (`FocalCodec`) do the opposite. --- ## 2. How BiSAT Works: Separate Continuous Spaces, One Shared Index ![BiSAT and BiSAT-TTS Overview](assets/overview.png) Inspired by TokenFlow's shared-index principle in image tokenization, **BiSAT** keeps acoustic and semantic representations **separate in continuous space** and couples them only through a **shared discrete index**: - **Dual 17-layer Conformer encoders** (initialized from NeMo `ssl_en_conformer_large`, 16 kHz → 25 Hz): the acoustic branch reconstructs log-mel spectrograms with pure $\ell_1$ loss (**no adversarial training**); the semantic branch sees SpecAugment-masked mel features and trains with **CTC** + layer-9 intermediate CTC. - **Shared-index Vector Quantization (SVQ):** Both encoder outputs and paired unit-normalized codebooks ($\boldsymbol{c}_a, \boldsymbol{c}_s \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times 512}$) pick **one shared index** per frame minimizing joint distance ($\omega = 1$): $$z_t = \arg\min_{k} \left[ \lVert \bar{\boldsymbol{e}}_{a,t} - \boldsymbol{c}_{k,a} \rVert_2^2 + \omega \lVert \bar{\boldsymbol{e}}_{s,t} - \boldsymbol{c}_{k,s} \rVert_2^2 \right]$$ - **Bidirectional alignment, no frozen teacher:** Neither encoder is frozen—updates in either branch shift shared assignments for both. - **100% / 99.8% codebook utilization at 32k / 64k:** Two-stage training (100k steps without VQ → spherical k-means init on 1.3M multilingual frames → 200k joint steps), **rotation trick**, shared-count EMA ($\eta = 0.99$), and dead-code reseeding every 100 steps yield **375 bps** (`BiSAT-32k`, 100% util.) and **400 bps** (`BiSAT-64k`, 99.8% util.). - **Clean downstream interface:** Training decoders are dropped at inference. Downstream LMs, acoustic decoders, and probes see **only the single integer sequence $\boldsymbol{z}_{1:T}$**. --- ## 3. Inside the Paired Codebooks ![Joint SVQ Trajectories](assets/codebook_diagnostics.png) - **Alignment converges (left):** Excess quantization distortion $r_b$ (the gap between shared index $z_t$ and each branch's own nearest entry) drops steadily from 50k to 200k steps and converges across both branches. - **Asymmetric geometric correspondence (right):** Directional information imbalance stays far below random $(1, 1)$ ($p = 0.005$); semantic neighbors map to tighter acoustic ranks ($\Delta(s \to a): 0.20 \to 0.17$ for $m = 1$), while acoustically similar frames naturally span distinct phonetic contexts ($\Delta(a \to s): 0.28 \to 0.36$). ![Task-wise TreeSHAP Attribution](assets/branch_shap.png) - **Clean branch specialization:** TreeSHAP attribution on frozen paired codebooks shows Pitch ($F_0$, **80.8%**) and Energy (**80.0%**) rely on $\boldsymbol{c}_a$, Phoneme Classification (**76.0%**) relies on $\boldsymbol{c}_s$, and Speaker ID (**71.0% / 29.0%**) and Emotion (**68.0% / 32.0%**) draw on both. --- ## 4. BiSAT-TTS: Zero-Shot TTS with 1/8th the Data **BiSAT-TTS** pairs a **MiniCPM4-0.5B** AR text-speech LM with a **22-block DiT** conditional flow-matching acoustic decoder (trained 50% offline / 50% chunk-causal for both offline and streaming decoding) and CosyVoice 3's frozen 24 kHz causal HiFT vocoder—trained on **122k hours** across 11 languages. ![BiSAT-TTS Zero-Shot Synthesis Benchmarks](assets/tts_benchmark.png) | System | Params | Data | LibriSpeech-PC WER ↓ | SIM-o ↑ | NISQA ↑ | Seed-TTS `test-en` WER ↓ | Seed-TTS `test-zh` CER ↓ | Fail ↓ | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | CosyVoice 2 | 500M | 167k h | 1.78% | 0.947 | **4.40** | 2.12% | 1.61% | 0.039% | | CosyVoice 3 | 500M | 1M h | 1.72% | **0.951** | 4.28 | 1.55% | 1.43% | 0.063% | | LLaSA-1B / 3B | 1B / 3B | 250k h | 2.00% / 2.17% | 0.930 / 0.931 | 4.23 / 4.22 | 1.91% / 2.38% | 2.27% / 1.69% | 0.409% / 0.512% | | **BiSAT-TTS-32k (PolyShift)** | **500M** | **122k h** | **1.50%** | 0.950 | 4.38 | 1.31% | 1.39% | 0.024% | | **BiSAT-TTS-64k (PolyShift)** | **500M** | **122k h** | 1.51% | 0.949 | 4.39 | **1.21%** | **1.27%** | **0.016%** | *3-seed averages (offline decoding, 10 Euler steps, CFG 0.7).* Listen to samples on our **[Audio Demo Page](https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo)**. --- ## 5. Limitations & Release Roadmap - **Multilingual & paralinguistic scope:** Both encoders start from an English SSL Conformer with far less Japanese/Mandarin data than CosyVoice 3's 1M-hour corpus (so Japanese ASR/reconstruction and Mandarin `SIM-o` still trail CosyVoice 3), and without paralinguistic labels, emotion recognition trails CosyVoice 3 (48.8% vs. 54.7% WA). - **Separate waveform decoder:** Unlike end-to-end codecs (`X-Codec2`), BiSAT relies on a separate speaker-conditioned flow-matching decoder and vocoder. ### Release Checklist - [x] Preprint on arXiv & Hugging Face Daily Papers ([arXiv:2611.30723](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.30723)) - [x] Audio Demo Page ([seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo](https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo)) - [ ] Open-source training & inference code - [ ] Pretrained weights for `BiSAT-32k`, `BiSAT-64k`, `BiSAT-TTS-32k`, and `BiSAT-TTS-64k` ## Citation ```bibtex @article{lu2026bisat, title={BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models}, author={Lu, Yixian and Wang, Lijun and Okada, Shogo}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.30723}, year={2026} } ```

[![GitHub](./assets/badges/github-badge.svg)](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS) [![License](./assets/badges/license-badge.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Demo](./assets/badges/demo-badge.svg)](https://edge0-ai.github.io/Audio8_TTS/realistic-0.6b/) [![arXiv](./assets/badges/arxiv-badge.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14776) [![Playground](./assets/badges/playground-badge.svg)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air) [Languages](#supported-languages) · [Quick start](#installation) · [Serving](#high-throughput-serving-sglang-omni) · [llama.cpp / GGUF](#native-local-inference-llamacpp) · [Evaluation](#evaluation)
> **2026-11-16 · llama.cpp / GGUF** — Native local inference, voice cloning and streaming for Realistic Air. Download the shared F32 bundle from [`llama-cpp/`](./llama-cpp/README.md). [Runbook](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/blob/0f8c4fade0cb14e38fbf737d0488553f16a0d658/guides/llama-cpp.md) · [中文](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/blob/0f8c4fade0cb14e38fbf737d0488553f16a0d658/guides/llama-cpp_zh.md). --- **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air** builds on [Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b), delivering **substantially improved speech realism** while retaining its compact **0.6B** architecture and zero-shot voice cloning capabilities. This release supports **23 languages**, adding **12 languages compared with Preview**. It uses the same Transformers inference interface as Preview. This repository includes the complete model checkpoint, its 44.1 kHz neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor, and custom Transformers code. Try speech generation and voice cloning in the [interactive Playground](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air). Hosted on Hugging Face ZeroGPU; availability depends on the queue and your daily GPU allowance. ## Highlights - **Improved realism:** more natural prosody and expressive delivery, building on Preview. - **Broader multilingual coverage:** 23 languages, including 12 additions to Preview's 11 supported languages. - **Compact model:** 601 million main-model parameters, with the audio codec bundled separately. - **Flexible generation:** zero-shot voice cloning from a reference recording and transcript, or speech generation without a reference. - **Native local deployment:** a llama.cpp integration with one shared F32 bundle, CLI, voice cloning and streaming. - **GPU serving:** an SGLang Omni adapter with paged attention, dynamic batching, and an OpenAI-compatible speech API. ## Supported Languages | Coverage | Languages | |---|---| | Supported in Preview (11) | Cantonese, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Spanish | | Added in Realistic Air (12) | Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese | > **Note:** Language quality varies; see the per-language evaluation below. Benchmark coverage includes some additional languages and is distinct from the supported-language list. ## Model Details Audio8 TTS uses a DualAR architecture inspired by [Fish Audio S2 Pro](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech). The slow AR transformer predicts one semantic token for each audio frame. The fast AR transformer predicts the frame's codec codebooks, conditioned on the slow hidden state and preceding codebooks. | Component | Configuration | |---|---| | Main model | 601,159,424 parameters, excluding the codec | | Slow AR | 24 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Fast AR | 4 layers, width 896, 14 attention heads, 2 KV heads | | Acoustic tokens | 10 codebooks, 4,096 entries per codebook | | Codec | 44.1 kHz, 2,048 samples per model frame (~21.5 frames/s) | | Context | Up to 2,048 packed text/audio positions | The bundled codec handles both reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding, so no additional codec checkpoint is required. The **0.6B** size refers to the main DualAR model; the codec is excluded from that parameter count. --- ## Installation Python 3.10 or newer and a CUDA-capable GPU are recommended. ```bash pip install "torch>=2.5.0" "torchaudio>=2.5.0" \ "transformers>=4.57.0,<5" "soundfile>=0.12" "safetensors>=0.4" ``` The Transformers release package was smoke-tested with PyTorch 2.8.0 and Transformers 4.57.3 on an NVIDIA H20 using BF16. Checks covered model loading, English and Chinese generation with and without reference audio, and generation in Arabic, Cantonese, Portuguese, and Russian. These are runtime checks, separate from the benchmark results below. ## Usage The model uses custom Transformers code. Review the files in this repository, then load it with `trust_remote_code=True`. ### Zero-shot voice cloning Use a clean reference recording. Its transcript must match the spoken content exactly. ```python import soundfile as sf import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor model_id = "Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air" device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu" dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == "cuda" else torch.float32 processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, dtype=dtype, ).eval().to(device) inputs = processor( text=["Welcome to Audio8 TTS. It is wonderful to hear from you."], reference_audio=["reference.wav"], reference_text=["The exact transcript of the reference recording."], return_tensors="pt", ) inputs = {name: value.to(device) for name, value in inputs.items()} with torch.inference_mode(): output = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95, top_k=50, do_sample=True, return_dict_in_generate=True, ) waveforms, waveform_lengths = model.decode_audio(output.codes) audio = waveforms[0, : int(waveform_lengths[0])].float().cpu().numpy() sf.write("output.wav", audio, model.config.codec_sample_rate) ``` ### Generation without a reference Replace the processor call above with: ```python inputs = processor( text=["This utterance does not use a reference voice."], return_tensors="pt", ) ``` Then move the inputs to the model device and run the same generation and decoding steps. For command-line inference, batching, and supervised fine-tuning, see the [Audio8 TTS repository](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS), using `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air` as the model path. ## High-throughput serving: SGLang Omni The [SGLang Omni adapter](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/master/sglang_omni) provides GPU serving for Audio8 TTS. It is installed as an independent model plugin and does not overwrite SGLang Omni core files. | Capability | Support | |---|---| | Attention and batching | SGLang paged attention and dynamic batching | | DualAR execution | Slow AR serving with a fixed KV cache for the Fast AR codebook decoder | | Voice cloning | Reference-audio encoding and waveform decoding | | API | OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` service | Use the **0.6B** configuration, `sglang_omni/configs/audio8_tts_0_6b.yaml`, and set the model path to `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air` or its downloaded snapshot. The adapter supports generation without a reference and zero-shot voice cloning. See the [deployment guide](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS#sglang-omni-serving) for compatible dependency versions, installation, server configuration, and API examples. > **Validation note:** Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air was tested on an NVIDIA H20 in BF16 for generation with and without a reference through the non-streaming speech API, with Torch compilation and CUDA graphs disabled. These checks validate runtime compatibility; throughput and streaming were not benchmarked. --- ## Native local inference: llama.cpp The native C++ integration provides local speech generation, reference-audio voice cloning, WAV output, HTTP and incremental streaming without Python, PyTorch or ONNX Runtime at inference time. Use the **Audio8 runtime and patch** linked below to load these model files. | Entry | Purpose | |---|---| | [Model folder](./llama-cpp/README.md) | Four F32 payloads (3.76 GB total), runtime manifest, checksums and licenses; shared unchanged across platforms | | [English runbook](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/blob/0f8c4fade0cb14e38fbf737d0488553f16a0d658/guides/llama-cpp.md) · [中文运行手册](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/blob/0f8c4fade0cb14e38fbf737d0488553f16a0d658/guides/llama-cpp_zh.md) | Download, build, generate, serve, stream, reproduce and troubleshoot | | [Source and converter](https://github.com/Edge0-AI/Audio8_TTS/tree/0f8c4fade0cb14e38fbf737d0488553f16a0d658/llama_cpp) | Fixed upstream patch, file verification and reproducible F32 export | F32 is the default. The same model files are used with each platform's runtime. ```bash hf download Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air \ --include "llama-cpp/**" --local-dir model/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air ``` Point the patched runtime's `--audio8-model-dir` at `model/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air/llama-cpp`, not at the Transformers root. Keep all four files and the metadata together. Whole-repository downloads for **Transformers/SGLang only** can use `--exclude "llama-cpp/**"` to avoid the extra GGUF download. The existing root checkpoint and Transformers interface are unchanged.
Note: Use CPU on macOS; Metal is experimental. The Windows build instructions have not yet been tested on a Windows machine.
--- ## Evaluation Error rates are percentages (**lower is better**). Speaker similarity (SIM) is on a **0–1 scale** (**higher is better**). These metrics measure intelligibility and speaker similarity; they do not directly measure perceived speech realism. ### Benchmark summary **Audio8-TTS-Preview** and **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air**, both **0.6B**: | Benchmark | Coverage | Preview error % ↓ | Realistic Air error % ↓ | Preview SIM ↑ | Realistic Air SIM ↑ | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Seed-TTS | English / Chinese | 1.23 | 1.25 | 0.682 | 0.704 | | CV3 | 8 shared languages | 4.80 | 4.56 | — | 0.663 | | CV3 | 9 core languages | — | 4.86 | — | 0.661 | | MiniMax | 24 evaluated languages | — | 5.89 | — | 0.754 | > **Note:** Values are unweighted language macro averages. Preview results are calculated from its [published model card](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b#evaluation), with SIM converted from percentages to a 0–1 scale. The two releases were evaluated separately. A dash means the corresponding result was not reported on Preview's card. > > Seed-TTS averages English WER and Chinese CER, excluding hard Chinese. The shared CV3 subset is Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, and Italian; the 9-language set also includes Russian. CV3 averages exclude hard subsets and the 13 additional languages. MiniMax averages all 24 evaluated languages, including languages outside the supported list. ### Reference comparison The following error rates come from the sources used in our technical report. Different evaluation pipelines and text normalization make this a reference comparison rather than a strictly matched ranking. A dash means that a result is unavailable in the comparison, not that the model lacks support. | Model | Parameters (B) | Seed-TTS EN/ZH error ↓ | CV3 (9) error ↓ | MiniMax (24) error ↓ | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air** | **0.6** | **1.25** | **4.86** | **5.89** | | Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B | 0.6 | 1.12 | — | — | | Qwen3-TTS-1.7B | 1.7 | 1.01 | 7.73 | 27.41 | | Higgs Audio v3 | 4 | 1.11 | 4.41 | 2.74 | | Higgs Audio v2 | 4.7 | 1.17 | 4.49 | — | | Fish S2 Pro | 4.6 | 1.32 | 4.49 | 4.40 | | MOSS-TTS-v1.5 | 8.5 | 1.52 | 6.11 | 3.78 | | CosyVoice3-1.5B | 1.5 | 1.67 | 6.89 | — | | VoxCPM2 | 2.3 | 1.41 | 5.35 | — | > **Sources:** Qwen Seed-TTS results are from the Qwen3-TTS report, linked from the [official Qwen3-TTS repository](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS); Qwen's CV3/MiniMax results, all Higgs Audio v3 results, and MOSS-TTS-v1.5's CV3/MiniMax results are from [Boson AI's evaluation](https://huggingface.co/bosonai/higgs-audio-v3-tts-4b). MOSS-TTS-v1.5's Seed-TTS result and the CosyVoice3/VoxCPM2 results are compiled in the [VoxCPM repository](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM). The remaining sizes are rounded checkpoint counts used in our report (VoxCPM2 excludes its separate AudioVAE). These counts use different conventions across systems. ### Seed-TTS detail | Split | Metric | Preview error % ↓ | Realistic Air error % ↓ | Preview SIM ↑ | Realistic Air SIM ↑ | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | English | WER | 1.506 | 1.464 | 0.632 | 0.663 | | Chinese | CER | 0.950 | 1.029 | 0.731 | 0.745 | | Chinese, hard | CER | 11.510 | 12.797 | 0.687 | 0.702 | > **Note:** Preview values are from its [published Seed-TTS table](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b#seed-tts), with SIM converted to a 0–1 scale. ### Multilingual detail

The detailed results include difficult cases, including Cantonese and some newly supported languages; the support list is not a claim of equal quality across languages. - Noisy reference audio or mismatched transcripts can reduce stability and speaker similarity. # Haru-4B GGUF (ROCmFPX)

GGUF files of [higurashi-ai/Haru-4B](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B), a full-duplex spoken dialogue
model by higurashi-ai, with a native C++ runtime (`llama-haru`) in the
[ROCmFPX fork of llama.cpp](https://github.com/HarshaVardhan3002/ROCmFPX).

Haru listens and speaks at the same time. Every 133 ms it takes one frame of your audio and produces one frame of
its own audio and text. The language model is a Qwen3.5-4B text backbone. A small MeanFlow head turns its hidden
state into a 64-dim audio latent, and a causal VibeVoice codec turns that into 24 kHz audio. All credit for the
model goes to higurashi-ai (and to the Qwen team for the backbone). See the
[original card](https://huggingface.co/higurashi-ai/Haru-4B) and the [Haru code](https://github.com/higurashi-ai/Haru).

## Files

| File | Size | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Haru-4B-Q8_0_ROCMFPX.gguf` | 4.37 GB | Language model, ROCmFPX 8-bit with tensor scales (needs the fork). Recommended |
| `Haru-4B-Q6_0_ROCMFPX.gguf` | 3.48 GB | Language model, ROCmFPX 6-bit with tensor scales (needs the fork) |
| `Haru-4B-audio-F16.gguf` | 2.30 GB | Audio parts: the two audio projectors, the MeanFlow head and the codec (needed with either model) |

You need one language model file and the audio file.

## Run it

Build the fork, then run an offline conversation from two WAV files (24 kHz mono):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HarshaVardhan3002/ROCmFPX && cd ROCmFPX
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build --target llama-haru -j

./build/bin/llama-haru -m Haru-4B-Q8_0_ROCMFPX.gguf --audio Haru-4B-audio-F16.gguf \
    --voice my_voice.wav --user question.wav --card-file card.txt -o answer.wav
```

- `--voice`: the voice Haru speaks with. One speaker, 3 seconds to 3 minutes, clean speech.
- `--user`: what you say. Haru listens to it frame by frame and answers while it plays.
- `--card` / `--card-file`: the character card (system prompt). The
  [Haru README](https://github.com/higurashi-ai/Haru) shows the card layout the model was trained with.
- Output: `answer.wav` (Haru's channel) and `answer-stereo.wav` (you on the left, Haru on the right).
  Haru's text appears on the terminal as it speaks.
- Sampling defaults follow the official code: temperature 0.7, top-k 25, guidance 1.5, DRY on.
  `--speak-first`, `--seed`, `--temp`, `--guidance` and `--tail` (seconds of listening after your clip) are available.

The runtime is an offline (file in, file out) tool for now. A live microphone mode is not part of this release.

## Accuracy

The runtime was checked part by part against the official PyTorch code in float32, on a real voice clip and
24 live dialogue frames:

| Part | Cosine similarity to PyTorch |
| --- | --- |
| Codec encode (whole clip and streaming), streaming decode | 1.000000 |
| Audio projectors (input embeddings) | 1.000000 |
| Language model hidden states | 0.999998 |
| Text logits | 0.999999 (same top token on 24 / 24 frames) |
| MeanFlow head latents | 1.000000 |

Quantized language models, KL divergence to BF16 on wiki text (40 x 512 tokens), and hidden-state similarity on the
real dialogue frames (file run as is on the CPU):

| Language model | Size | Wiki KLD | Dialogue hidden cosine |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q8_0_ROCMFPX (this repo) | 4.37 GB | 0.0019 | 0.9966 |
| stock Q8_0 (not uploaded) | 4.48 GB | 0.0031 | 0.9954 |
| Q6_0_ROCMFPX (this repo) | 3.48 GB | 0.0113 | 0.9915 |
| stock Q6_K (not uploaded) | 3.46 GB | 0.0153 | 0.9913 |

On the CPU, use the fork at commit `4310e2480` or newer for the ROCmFPX 8-bit file. Older builds rounded the
activations to 8 bits before each matrix multiply, which brought this file down to 0.966 on the dialogue frames.
The audio file in F16 matches the float32 one (head cosine 0.9999997).

## Notes and limits

- Verified on the CPU (ARM). On a CPU it is slower than real time; real-time use needs a GPU build. GPU backends
  have not been tested with this runtime yet.
- Haru-4B is a pretrained base model released for research. It holds a natural conversation, but it is not a
  reliable source of facts and does not follow instructions the way an assistant does.
- It can imitate the voice of a reference clip. Only use voices you have the right to use.

V3 is designed for broad language coverage like V2, but with stronger stability and more expressive generation. It is the recommended multilingual model for users who want one voice cloning model that works across many languages. Chatterbox Multilingual supports **Arabic, Danish, German, Greek, English, Spanish, Finnish, French, Hebrew, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Dutch, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Swahili, Turkish, Chinese** out of the box. Licensed under MIT, Chatterbox has been benchmarked against leading closed-source systems like ElevenLabs, and is consistently preferred in side-by-side evaluations. Whether you're working on memes, videos, games, or AI agents, Chatterbox brings your content to life. It's also the first open source TTS model to support **emotion exaggeration control**, a powerful feature that makes your voices stand out. Try it now on our [Hugging Face Gradio app.](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ResembleAI/Chatterbox) If you like the model but need to scale or tune it for higher accuracy, check out our competitively priced TTS service (link). It delivers reliable performance with ultra-low latency of sub 200ms—ideal for production use in agents, applications, or interactive media. # Key Details - Chatterbox Multilingual V3, a 0.5B general-purpose multilingual TTS model supporting 23 languages - Dedicated single-language finetunes for Chinese, LatAm Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Spain Spanish, Portugal Portuguese, and Hindi - SoTA zeroshot English TTS - 0.5B Llama backbone - Unique exaggeration/intensity control - Ultra-stable with alignment-informed inference - Trained on 0.5M hours of cleaned data - Watermarked outputs - Easy voice conversion script - [Outperforms ElevenLabs](https://podonos.com/resembleai/chatterbox) # Tips - **General Use (TTS and Voice Agents):** - The default settings (`exaggeration=0.5`, `cfg=0.5`) work well for most prompts. - If the reference speaker has a fast speaking style, lowering `cfg` to around `0.3` can improve pacing. - **Expressive or Dramatic Speech:** - Try lower `cfg` values (e.g. `~0.3`) and increase `exaggeration` to around `0.7` or higher. - Higher `exaggeration` tends to speed up speech; reducing `cfg` helps compensate with slower, more deliberate pacing. ***Note:*** Ensure that the reference clip matches the specified language tag. Otherwise, language transfer outputs may inherit the accent of the reference clip’s language. ***To mitigate this, set the CFG weight to 0.*** # Installation ``` pip install chatterbox-tts ``` # Usage ```python import torchaudio as ta from chatterbox.tts import ChatterboxTTS model = ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device="cuda") text = "Ezreal and Jinx teamed up with Ahri, Yasuo, and Teemo to take down the enemy's Nexus in an epic late-game pentakill." wav = model.generate(text) ta.save("test-1.wav", wav, model.sr) # If you want to synthesize with a different voice, specify the audio prompt AUDIO_PROMPT_PATH="YOUR_FILE.wav" wav = model.generate(text, audio_prompt_path=AUDIO_PROMPT_PATH) ta.save("test-2.wav", wav, model.sr) ``` # Multilingual Quickstart ```python import torchaudio as ta from chatterbox.mtl_tts import ChatterboxMultilingualTTS multilingual_model = ChatterboxMultilingualTTS.from_pretrained( device="cuda", t3_model="v3", ) # To use the legacy V2 multilingual checkpoint, omit t3_model or pass t3_model="v2". french_text = "Bonjour, comment ça va? Ceci est le modèle de synthèse vocale multilingue Chatterbox, il prend en charge 23 langues." wav_french = multilingual_model.generate(french_text, language_id="fr") ta.save("test-french.wav", wav_french, multilingual_model.sr) chinese_text = "你好，今天天气真不错，希望你有一个愉快的周末。" wav_chinese = multilingual_model.generate(chinese_text, language_id="zh") ta.save("test-chinese.wav", wav_chinese, multilingual_model.sr) ``` See `example_tts.py` for more examples. ## Single Language Pack The Single Language Pack provides dedicated finetunes for priority languages and regional variants. models.card_text: --- language: - zh - en - ar - my - da - nl - fi - fr - de - el - he - hi - id - it - ja - km - ko - lo - ms - no - pl - pt - ru - es - sw - sv - tl - th - tr - vi license: apache-2.0 library_name: voxcpm tags: - text-to-speech - tts - multilingual - voice-cloning - voice-design - diffusion - audio pipeline_tag: text-to-speech --- # VoxCPM2 **VoxCPM2** is a tokenizer-free, diffusion autoregressive Text-to-Speech model — **2B parameters**, **30 languages**, **48kHz** audio output, trained on over **2 million hours** of multilingual speech data. [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-VoxCPM-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docs-ReadTheDocs-8CA1AF)](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live%20Playground-Demo-orange)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/OpenBMB/VoxCPM-Demo) [![Audio Samples](https://img.shields.io/badge/Audio%20Samples-Demo%20Page-green)](https://openbmb.github.io/voxcpm2-demopage) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-VoxCPM-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/KZUx7tVNwz) [![Lark](https://img.shields.io/badge/飞书群-VoxCPM-00D6B9?logo=lark&logoColor=white)](https://applink.feishu.cn/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=acds0b9d-23d8-4d7e-b696-d200f3e22a7f) [![MiniCPM Wiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/MiniCPM-Wiki-1677FF?logo=readthedocs&logoColor=white)](https://openbmb.cn/docs/) ## Highlights - 🌍 **30-Language Multilingual** — No language tag needed; input text in any supported language directly - 🎨 **Voice Design** — Generate a novel voice from a natural-language description alone (gender, age, tone, emotion, pace…); no reference audio required - 🎛️ **Controllable Cloning** — Clone any voice from a short clip, with optional style guidance to steer emotion, pace, and expression while preserving timbre - 🎙️ **Ultimate Cloning** — Provide reference audio + its transcript for audio-continuation cloning; every vocal nuance faithfully reproduced - 🔊 **48kHz Studio-Quality Output** — Accepts 16kHz reference; outputs 48kHz via AudioVAE V2's built-in super-resolution, no external upsampler needed - 🧠 **Context-Aware Synthesis** — Automatically infers appropriate prosody and expressiveness from text content - ⚡ **Real-Time Streaming** — RTF as low as ~0.3 on NVIDIA RTX 4090, and ~0.13 accelerated by [Nano-VLLM](https://github.com/a710128/nanovllm-voxcpm) - 📜 **Fully Open-Source & Commercial-Ready** — Apache-2.0 license, free for commercial use Supported Languages (30) Arabic, Burmese, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Lao, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tagalog, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese Chinese Dialects: 四川话, 粤语, 吴语, 东北话, 河南话, 陕西话, 山东话, 天津话, 闽南话 ## Quick Start ### Installation ```bash pip install voxcpm ``` **Requirements:** Python ≥ 3.10, PyTorch ≥ 2.5.0, CUDA ≥ 12.0 · [Full Quick Start →](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart.html) ### Text-to-Speech ```python from voxcpm import VoxCPM import soundfile as sf model = VoxCPM.from_pretrained("openbmb/VoxCPM2", load_denoiser=False) wav = model.generate( text="VoxCPM2 brings multilingual support, creative voice design, and controllable voice cloning.", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("output.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Voice Design Put the voice description in parentheses at the start of `text`, followed by the content to synthesize: ```python wav = model.generate( text="(A young woman, gentle and sweet voice)Hello, welcome to VoxCPM2!", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("voice_design.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Controllable Voice Cloning ```python # Basic cloning wav = model.generate( text="This is a cloned voice generated by VoxCPM2.", reference_wav_path="speaker.wav", ) sf.write("clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) # Cloning with style control wav = model.generate( text="(slightly faster, cheerful tone)This is a cloned voice with style control.", reference_wav_path="speaker.wav", cfg_value=2.0, inference_timesteps=10, ) sf.write("controllable_clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Ultimate Cloning Provide both the reference audio and its exact transcript for maximum fidelity. Pass the same clip to both `reference_wav_path` and `prompt_wav_path` for highest similarity: ```python wav = model.generate( text="This is an ultimate cloning demonstration using VoxCPM2.", prompt_wav_path="speaker_reference.wav", prompt_text="The transcript of the reference audio.", reference_wav_path="speaker_reference.wav", ) sf.write("hifi_clone.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ### Streaming ```python import numpy as np chunks = [] for chunk in model.generate_streaming(text="Streaming is easy with VoxCPM!"): chunks.append(chunk) wav = np.concatenate(chunks) sf.write("streaming.wav", wav, model.tts_model.sample_rate) ``` ## Model Details | Property | Value | |---|---| | Architecture | Tokenizer-free Diffusion Autoregressive (LocEnc → TSLM → RALM → LocDiT) | | Backbone | Based on MiniCPM-4, totally 2B parameters | | Audio VAE | AudioVAE V2 (asymmetric encode/decode, 16kHz in → 48kHz out) | | Training Data | 2M+ hours multilingual speech | | LM Token Rate | 6.25 Hz | | Max Sequence Length | 8192 tokens | | dtype | bfloat16 | | VRAM | ~8 GB | | RTF (RTX 4090) | ~0.30 (standard) / ~0.13 (Nano-vLLM) | ## Performance VoxCPM2 achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on major zero-shot and controllable TTS benchmarks. See the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM#-performance) for full benchmark tables (Seed-TTS-eval, CV3-eval, InstructTTSEval, MiniMax Multilingual Test). ## Fine-tuning VoxCPM2 supports both full SFT and LoRA fine-tuning with as little as 5–10 minutes of audio: ```bash # LoRA fine-tuning (recommended) python scripts/train_voxcpm_finetune.py \ --config_path conf/voxcpm_v2/voxcpm_finetune_lora.yaml # Full fine-tuning python scripts/train_voxcpm_finetune.py \ --config_path conf/voxcpm_v2/voxcpm_finetune_all.yaml ``` See the [Fine-tuning Guide](https://voxcpm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/finetuning/finetune.html) for full instructions. ## Limitations - Voice Design and Style Control results may vary between runs; generating 1–3 times is recommended to obtain the desired output. - Performance varies across languages depending on training data availability. - Occasional instability may occur with very long or highly expressive inputs. - **Strictly forbidden** to use for impersonation, fraud, or disinformation. AI-generated content should be clearly labeled. ## Citation ```bibtex @article{voxcpm2_2026, title = {VoxCPM2: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Multilingual Speech Generation, Creative Voice Design, and True-to-Life Cloning}, author = {VoxCPM Team}, journal = {GitHub}, year = {2026}, } @article{voxcpm2025, title = {VoxCPM: Tokenizer-Free TTS for Context-Aware Speech Generation and True-to-Life Voice Cloning}, author = {Zhou, Yixuan and Zeng, Guoyang and Liu, Xin and Li, Xiang and Yu, Renjie and Wang, Ziyang and Ye, Runchuan and Sun, Weiyue and Gui, Jiancheng and Li, Kehan and Wu, Zhiyong and Liu, Zhiyuan}, journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.24650}, year = {2025}, } ``` ## License Released under the [Apache-2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) license, free for commercial use. For production deployments, we recommend thorough testing and safety evaluation tailored to your use case.

# OmniVoice for WebGPU (ONNX)

[OmniVoice](https://huggingface.co/k2-fsa/OmniVoice) by k2-fsa, converted to run inside a web browser with
ONNX Runtime Web. It is what [FreeGen](https://freegen.ai)'s Speak studio downloads for voice cloning and
voice design. Nothing is uploaded: the text, any reference clip, and the speech stay on the visitor's machine.

OmniVoice speaks 600+ languages, clones a voice from a few seconds of audio, and designs one from attributes
(gender, age, pitch, whisper, accent). It is a Qwen3-0.6B run bidirectionally as a masked language model over
eight codebooks of the Higgs Audio 2 codec: a clip starts fully masked and 32 passes fill it in, each guided
by a second, unconditioned pass.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `step_int4.onnx` (+ `.data`, 453 MB) | One pass: `input_ids` [B, 8, S], `audio_mask` [B, S], `attention_mask` [B, 1, S, S] -> `logits` [B, 8, S, 1025]. Exported from the official checkpoint with the mask given explicitly (bidirectional); int4 matrices (MatMulNBits, block 32) and int8 embedding rows looked up with plain Gather, so it also runs on the processor. Against the fp32 export: cosine 0.9997 |
| `higgs_audio_2_tokenizer/higgs_decoder.onnx` (43 MB, fp16) | Codes [8, 1, T] -> 24 kHz audio. 64 dB from PyTorch |
| `higgs_audio_2_tokenizer/{acoustic,semantic,quantizer}_encoder.onnx` (654 MB, fp32) | A reference clip -> codes, for cloning only. Same codes as PyTorch |
| `tokenizer.json`, `languages.json`, `omnivoice-pack.json` | Qwen tokenizer, the 646 language ids, the manifest |

The prompt, duration estimate, schedule, guidance and sampling are host code, ported from
`omnivoice/models/omnivoice.py`: FreeGen's `src/freegen/omnivoice.js`. The export is `scripts/omnivoice-export.py`.
The codec graphs come from [onnx-community/OmniVoice-Onnx](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/OmniVoice-Onnx).

## Credits and licences

- OmniVoice by k2-fsa (Xiaomi), Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`).

# SpeechExpert-Wav2Vec2-Deepfake

A compact Speech Expert model for detecting signs of synthetic speech in audio. It uses a four-layer wav2vec2 encoder, mean and standard deviation pooling, and a binary classification head. The model was trained on natural and synthetic speech with replay augmentation.

This release contains the standalone wav2vec2 detector. The [Speech Expert web detector](https://speech-expert.ru/free-tools/voice-deepfake/) combines several models and checks for an ElevenLabs watermark. This ONNX file produces one acoustic score per input phrase.

## Model interface

| Tensor | Shape for one phrase | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `waveform` | `[1, samples]` | Float32, mono, 16 kHz |
| `probs` | `[1, 2]` | Float32, in the order `[orig, synth]` |

Use `probs[0, 1]` as the synthetic-speech score. The model already returns softmax scores. For each complete phrase, keep its pauses, convert to mono at 16 kHz, subtract the mean, and scale by the absolute peak only if it exceeds 1. The time axis is dynamic. The reference client allows 400–480,000 samples (25 ms–30 s), with one phrase per call. The 25 ms limit is a technical minimum. Use an intelligible speech phrase for analysis.

## Run locally

Install `huggingface_hub`, `numpy`, `onnxruntime`, `scipy`, and `soundfile`. Set `phrase.wav` to a file containing one speech phrase. The example downloads `config.json` and the ONNX weights from the same revision.

```python
import json
from math import gcd
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import onnxruntime as ort
import soundfile as sf
from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from scipy.signal import resample_poly

model_dir = Path(snapshot_download(
    "Strij911/SpeechExpert-Wav2Vec2-Deepfake",
    allow_patterns=["config.json", "model.onnx"],
))
config = json.loads((model_dir / "config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
session = ort.InferenceSession(
    str(model_dir / config["model_file"]), providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"],
)

audio, rate = sf.read("phrase.wav", dtype="float32", always_2d=True)
audio = audio.mean(axis=1, dtype=np.float32)
target_rate = config["sample_rate"]
if rate != target_rate:
    divisor = gcd(rate, target_rate)
    audio = resample_poly(audio, target_rate // divisor, rate // divisor)
if not config["min_samples"] <= audio.size <= config["max_samples"] or not np.isfinite(audio).all():
    raise ValueError("Expected a valid phrase of at most 30 seconds.")
audio = np.asarray(audio, dtype=np.float32)
audio -= audio.mean(dtype=np.float32)
peak = np.max(np.abs(audio))
if peak > 1:
    audio /= peak

waveform = np.ascontiguousarray(audio[None, :], dtype=np.float32)
scores = session.run([config["output_name"]], {config["input_name"]: waveform})[0][0]
print(dict(zip(config["labels"], map(float, scores), strict=True)))
```

## Evaluation and limitations

The checkpoint-selection validation contained 5,999 recordings. Under the historical evaluation protocol, which trimmed leading and trailing non-speech and averaged results over five 2-second crops, the model obtained 97.56% ROC AUC, 7.70% EER, and 91.63% accuracy at a 0.5 threshold. These are checkpoint-selection results. Performance and calibration under whole-phrase inference require a separate evaluation on representative data.

Use the output as a signal for review. Unseen generators, codecs, recording conditions, and short or mixed clips can yield errors. The score does not establish who spoke, which system produced the clip, or whether a recording is authentic. Test thresholds on data representative of your use case.

## Artifact

- `model.onnx` contains all weights in a single file. ONNX IR 8, opset 17.
- 6,450,114 parameters, 25,900,262 bytes.
- SHA-256 `661d8da3976acc4b5226472906a568d0db8a4b739fce6a0d082d724d42871c6b`.

## Кратко по-русски

Модель Speech Expert оценивает признаки синтетической речи по отдельной фразе. Подайте моно-аудио 16 кГц и используйте выход `probs[0, 1]` как оценку синтеза. Результат относится ко всей поданной фразе. Для проверки длинной записи с таймкодами можно воспользоваться [веб-детектором Speech Expert](https://speech-expert.ru/free-tools/voice-deepfake/).
